title: Thinking Loop v2: checks, captures, threats

D0.outcome: States the order in which forcing moves are examined (checks, captures, direct threats) for both sides and why forcing moves go first.

D1.outcome: Lists every check, capture and direct threat for the side to move, and for the opponent in the position after a quiet move.

D2.outcome: In unlabeled positions, finds the forcing move that works when one exists, and says that no forcing move helps when none does.

D3.outcome: Examines the opponent's best forcing reply to each forcing candidate (a check answered by a check, a capture met by an in-between move) before choosing.

D4.outcome: In own games, a sampled log shows forcing moves of both sides listed before the move in critical positions, with prompts off.

misconceptions: Only my own forcing moves matter; the opponent's can wait.
A capture that wins material on the first move is always correct.

conditions: Used when the position is not quiet or when the opponent's last move was forcing.

contrasts: A first-move capture whose recapture comes with check, leaving the capturer worse.
Listing only forcing moves for the side to move and missing the opponent's check in reply.
A quiet position with no checks or captures available for either side; the list is empty.
